services.name: Past Exhibits
services.desc: LGBTQ2S+ people have always existed on the prairies: Two-Spirit (niizh manidoowag) people have lived here long before European settlers arrived, with numerous accounts of First Nations who had same-sex partners or did not conform to traditional gender roles. Unfortunately, with the arrival of settlers, colonial homophobia and gender discrimination were introduced to the prairies and are rampant still today, even after Pierre Trudeau’s government partially decriminalized homosexuality in 1969. This exhibit explores the activism that took place in Saskatchewan from the late 1960s through the summer of 2020. Journey through the stories of lesbian and gay activists and groups of the 1960-1980s

services.desc: The Diefenbaker Spy Academy: Super Sleuths Calling all secret agents! Become a spy-in-training at the super-secret Diefenbaker Spy Academy (DSA). Daily briefings from the DSA Director will provide you with the skills you need to create a cover identity, crack secret codes, design your own spy gear, and so much more!

services.desc: Solve this crossword and learn about the strength and resilience that helped Mennonites of Saskatchewan to survive when immigrating to Canada from Europe. Find the answers for this crossword in the Diefenbaker Canada Centre's online exhibit, Flight and Resilience: Mennonites of Saskatchewan. Suitable for ages 11+.
